title: Colorimetric sulfo-phospho-vanillin (SPV) method for analysis of lipids in mucin
author: Xueying Zhong
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.euybexw
materials: Then add 1.25 ml chloroform and vortex well;

steps.title: Prepare mucin sample solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the mucins in water to the predetermined concentration required for the assay.

steps.title: Extract lipids from mucin
steps.instruction: Perform a liquid–liquid extraction on each 1 mL of mucin sample solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 3.75 mL of a 1:2 (v/v) chloroform:methanol mixture and vortex thoroughly.
Add 1.25 mL chloroform and vortex again.
Add 1.25 mL dH₂O and vortex again.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1000 RPM for 5 min to obtain a two‑phase system (aqueous top, organic bottom).
Recover the bottom (organic) phase with a Pasteur pipette and transfer to a clean tube.

steps.title: Prepare cholesterol standard solutions
steps.instruction: Create a series of cholesterol standards in a 2:1 chloroform:methanol solvent.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the solvent mixture of chloroform:methanol at a 2:1 volume ratio.
Dissolve cholesterol in this solvent to a concentration of approximately 5 mg mL⁻¹.
Aliquot varying volumes of the cholesterol solution (1 µL, 2 µL, 4 µL, 8 µL, 16 µL, and 24 µL) into separate tubes to generate standards with different cholesterol amounts.

steps.title: Evaporate solvents from samples
steps.instruction: Dry the organic extracts from the mucin samples and all cholesterol standard tubes to remove chloroform/methanol solvent.

steps.title: Prepare sulfo‑phospho‑vanillin reagent
steps.instruction: Make the color‑development reagent by dissolving 0.2 mg vanillin per mL of 17 % phosphoric acid.

steps.title: Add reagent for color development
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the sulfo‑phospho‑vanillin reagent to each dried sample (both standards and extracts).

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 540 nm
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction for 5 min to allow color development, then record the absorbance at 540 nm.
